title: Publicly financed candidates and the outside money spent for them
question: For candidates who took public financing, how much did outside committees report spending to support them?
finding: In the elections of 2012-2020 covered by the third-party disclosure summaries, 60 candidate races took $11,186,502 in public financing, and outside committees reported $7,850,831 of spending to support those same candidates. In 14 races the outside support was larger than the public money. The two largest: London Breed, June 2018, $975,000 public and $1,275,240 outside, most of it from the committee sponsored by Firefighters Local 798; Ahsha Safaí, November 2016, $145,743 public and $780,327 outside.
how: Public funds approved (dbak-p2fq) summed by election and candidate; third-party disclosures (ani6-nqh6, the combined summary of independent expenditures, member communications and electioneering communications) summed by the same key, support and oppose separately. Candidates are matched on surname and the first three letters of the first name within one election.
limits: The disclosure summaries are compiled by hand by the Ethics Commission and cover only publicly financed contests in 2011 to 2020; spending reported after the summary was compiled is missing. Outside spending is by law independent of the candidate, and a candidate cannot refuse it. Approved public funds can differ slightly from funds paid.
